must_remember: The vector average velocity of gas molecules in a stationary container is identically zero ($v_{av} = 0$) due to isotropic random motion.
Mean speed ($v_{bar}$), root-mean-square speed ($v_{rms}$), and most probable speed ($v_{mp}$) are all non-zero scalar quantities.
The hierarchy of characteristic speeds is always $v_{mp} < v_{bar} < v_{rms}$.
Characteristic molecular speeds vary directly with the square root of absolute temperature ($v \propto \sqrt{T}$) and inversely with the square root of molar mass ($v \propto 1/\sqrt{M}$).

glossary.meaning: The arithmetic mean of individual molecular velocity vectors, which equals zero for a gas at rest.
The arithmetic mean of the scalar magnitudes of molecular speeds, given by $\sqrt{\frac{8RT}{\pi M}}$.
The square root of the average of squared speeds, given by $\sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}}$.
The speed possessed by the maximum fraction of molecules at a given temperature, given by $\sqrt{\frac{2RT}{M}}$.
